title: Correlated Coherent Errors in Stabilizer Codes: A General Cumulant Framework and Interference-Based Error Suppression
authors: Rohan N Rajmohan, Antoine Brillant, Peter Groszkowski, Alireza Seif, Jens Koch, Aashish Clerk
abstract: Coherent errors in stabilizer codes are often correlated across qubits and QEC cycles. Having a general analytical treatment of such noise would thus be extremely valuable. We derive here the exact logical channel induced by repeated QEC cycles under correlated coherent $Z$ noise, and develop a broadly general cumulant-expansion framework that yields a tractable expression for the noise-averaged logical infidelity. Crucially, this expression is non-perturbative in the noise, and applies to arbitrary stabilizer codes and correlation structures. It reveals a feature with no analogue in standard stochastic Pauli error models: the induced channel depends on which stabilizer eigenspace is chosen as the codespace. Exploiting this, we introduce protected stabilizer eigenspace (PROSE) encoding, an error-suppression strategy that selects the optimal codespace. We show that this eigenspace can be efficiently identified in many relevant situations. Further, when combined with logical Pauli twirling, PROSE matches or outperforms standard error suppression techniques (dynamical decoupling, Pauli twirling of physical qubits). We also show that noise correlations, usually assumed to be harmful to QEC, can instead be a resource: with the right encoding, even positive correlations reduce the logical infidelity below the uncorrelated baseline. Our results offer a new, broadly applicable lens on correlated coherent noise in stabilizer codes.
summary: This work provides a comprehensive theoretical framework for analyzing how correlated coherent errors affect stabilizer codes during QEC. By developing the PROSE encoding strategy, the authors show that selecting the optimal codespace can actively suppress these structured errors. Crucially, they demonstrate that positive noise correlations, often viewed as detrimental, can actually be harnessed as a resource to improve error correction performance.
main_problem: The paper develops a general analytical framework to treat correlated coherent errors occurring during repeated Quantum Error Correction (QEC) cycles in stabilizer codes.
main_result: It introduces Protected Stabilizer Eigenspace (PROSE) encoding, which can exploit noise correlations to reduce logical infidelity below the level predicted by uncorrelated error models. Furthermore, PROSE combined with Pauli twirling matches or outperforms standard error suppression techniques.
method: The authors derive the exact logical channel using a general cumulant-expansion framework, yielding a non-perturbative expression for the noise-averaged logical infidelity.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is quantum information encoded in stabilizer codes. The noise model specifically considers correlated coherent dephasing errors (Z-noise) acting on data qubits during each QEC cycle.
key_observables: Logical infidelity ($\epsilon(R)$), which quantifies the error rate after $R$ cycles, and the dependence of the induced channel on the chosen stabilizer eigenspace.
important_parameters: The noise correlation structure (positive correlations are shown to be beneficial), the number of QEC cycles ($R$), and the strength of coherent errors ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the syndrome measurement and recovery operations within a single QEC cycle are noiseless. The derivations rely on cumulant expansions, which provide analytical insight into the noise average.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate quantum circuits for multiple QEC cycles with coherent Z errors; captions highlight how positive noise correlations can reduce logical infidelity below the uncorrelated baseline when using PROSE encoding.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first deriving the exact channel under correlated noise, then developing the general cumulant framework. It introduces PROSE encoding based on the dependence of the channel on the codespace choice. Finally, it compares PROSE+twirling against standard techniques like dynamical decoupling and Pauli twirling.
why_interesting: The ability to treat structured, non-Markovian noise (coherent errors) analytically is highly valuable for designing robust quantum hardware protocols, especially in superconducting or trapped-ion platforms where correlated noise sources are common.
